title: Schema-led replayable fragment envelopes: SDK examples and compatibility shims
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a compact, deterministic pattern for emitting incremental/fragmented JSON responses that: (1) clearly delineates tool/function call boundaries, (2) can be validated against schema fragments at emit-time, (3) supports deterministic replay/rehydration on the client side, and (4) requires minimal changes to existing streaming SDKs (TS/Py/Go).

Goal: Deliver cross-language reference implementations and lightweight compatibility shims showing a contract-first framing for streamed fragments. Provide examples, docs, a migration guide, and tests demonstrating round-trip rehydration.

Design sketch: Use newline-delimited JSON envelope records. Each envelope has: id, type (fragment|tool|end), schema (URI), body (JSON|null), seq (int). The final envelope includes a replay_root_id for server-side replay if fragments were missed. Clients apply fragments in seq order to rehydrate the final object. SDKs offer compatibility mode to wrap legacy streams into the envelope model by heuristically detecting JSON boundaries or function markers.

Language examples (high level):
- TypeScript: parseFragmentStream(stream: AsyncIterable<string>) -> AsyncIterable<FragmentEnvelope>; assembleFromFragments(frags) validates against AJV and returns final object; helpers to emit tool start/result envelopes.
- Python: parse_fragments(generator) yields fragment dicts; Rehydrator class with apply_fragment(fragment) and finalize() methods; compatibility shim that wraps legacy generators.
- Go: FragmentEnvelope struct with json.RawMessage body; ParseFragments(r io.Reader) returns channel of envelopes; Rehydrator with deterministic merge semantics based on schema tags.

Trade-offs: Per-fragment schema URIs increase wire size but simplify validation and evolution. Sequence numbers support out-of-order delivery; no CRDT merges. Replay endpoint reuses existing auth tokens and TTLs. Compatibility shims are opt-in to avoid changing legacy client behavior unexpectedly.

Acceptance criteria and deliverables are listed below and must be met before merge.
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go examples with parser, rehydrator, tool helpers, and unit tests are present in examples/sdk-fragment-replay
End-to-end demo: runtime emits fragmented response with a tool call; client rehydrates and validates final object
Benchmarks show <=5% throughput regression on common small-fragment workloads
Migration guide and compatibility shim for legacy streams are included
SDK owners (TS/Py/Go) and Product sign off on API surface and compatibility guidance
